prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: システム連携用語表 (language ja).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "用語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 210px
  col 2: header "英語" · longest unbreakable word 103px · one-line width 163px
  col 3: header "説明" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 860px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Row-header column is wide enough that every Japanese term stays on one line, so the identifiers readers scan first are intact; the English column wraps only at word spaces (transaction / manager), and the description column gets roughly 300px, giving steady 2–3 line paragraphs. Rhythm across the three columns is even, nothing is orphaned, and rows read as compact units."},"B":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Essentially the same balanced allocation as A, with the description column a touch wider (breaks fall after でき/提供 rather than mid-clause), so prose lines are slightly more even while the term column still holds every entry unbroken. English phrases break cleanly at spaces; hierarchy and vertical rhythm look consistent."},"C":{"grade":"poor","why":"The term column is squeezed to about 175px, so katakana entries break with one- or two-character orphans (…マネージ／ャー, …レー／ション, …プロバイ／ダー, …アグリーメン／ト). Those broken identifiers are exactly what a reader uses to find a row, and the extra width does not visibly improve the description column, so the trade is a net loss."},"D":{"grade":"poor","why":"The English column is over-generous (long phrases on one line) at the expense of the description, which is squeezed to about 235px and now runs 5–6 short, ragged lines per row, including a lone ト。 and コンポーネン／ト. Rows become very tall and uneven, and the table loses its scanning rhythm; the smallest-information column takes space the largest one needs."},"E":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Very close to A/B: terms stay whole on one line, English wraps only at spaces, and the description column carries the bulk of the width with consistent 2–3 line paragraphs. Slightly more slack in the English column than strictly needed, but no word breaks and no orphan lines, so the reading order term → English → description stays clean."},"F":{"grade":"poor","why":"The term column is cut to about 160px, splitting core terms mid-word (インターホペラ／ビリティ, トランザクショ／ンマネージャー, アイデンティテ／ィプロバイダー, サービスレベル／アグリーメント). Row headers stop being recognizable at a glance, and the description still only gains a little width, so the cost is high for little benefit."}},"best":["A","B","E"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"A, B and E look nearly identical at this scale (differences of ~10px per column, only visible in where a description line breaks), so ranking them against each other is within measurement error; the clear signal is that C, D and F each sacrifice a column that matters (row-header integrity in C/F, description width in D). I also cannot verify exact pixel boundaries from the images, only relative proportions."}
